findings.reason: making the guard real costs one clause in §3's done-when (or one `s3` gate) naming `tests/test_cited_commands_exist.py` green after the rewrite, without which §5's stated purpose for running first and its table hand-off are both unenforced.
findings.text: §5 hands §3 two outcomes it does not measure — the guard of §5's test over §3's rewrite, and the fix of the `coordinator-reference.md` table that §5 found stale — while §3's done-when (`the-crew-contract-fits-one-read.html:66-70`) requires only the 12,000-word ceiling, the parity tests and the token measure, and the only two `s3` gates (`:82-90`) cite `a-refusal-is-about-the-work` and `a-review-is-sized-to-its-risk`, neither being this test — so §3 can rewrite `SKILL.md` and the references and land a dead citation or the five-command-short table with nothing failing

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `PLAN-FORMAT.md:321`/`:330`, `sprint-orchestration.md:1011`, `references/coordinator-reference.md:593-614`, and `SKILL.md:185-211` each resolve to the content §5 names, and §5 carries no extensionless href to resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when is measurable and names both a positive control (the test fails at this section's base naming three citations) and a negative control (a temporary skill file citing `reckon crew dispatch --no-such-flag` fails by file and line), so its guard can be shown to fire.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 cites the durable health-review report directory under `~/.config/reckon/crew/reports/...`, and names no session scratchpad, node-local temporary path, or non-surviving location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces no symbol, file or comment carrying a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; `807053fb6` and the review date are provenance in a document, not names in code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5 asserts its test "then guards §3's rewrite of `SKILL.md` and the references: every command the rewritten text cites must still resolve", and defers the drifted command table to "§3, which rewrites that file", but §3's done-when names only the word ceiling, `tests/test_skill_contract_parity.py` and the token measure, and no gate with `data-gated-sections="s3"` runs `test_cited_commands_exist.py` — so the guard and the table fix §5 relies on §3 to deliver are carried by no §3 measure.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — the section has one goal, that every cited command resolve; the command-table replacement that earlier sat in the deliverable is now removed and named as §3's.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 declares its own ordering ("This section runs before §3") and the section it guards, and no relationship points at a node that does not exist; the residual is that the guard is not represented as a measure, raised under reasoning.
